title: Quiz 3
topic: CNNs, Pooling, Stride & Feature Engineering – Weeks 3 & 4

questions.text: Activation functions are used in a neural network to compute the net input to the neuron and they add non-linearity to the network.
questions.feedback: Activation functions add non-linearity, but they do NOT compute the net input — that is done by the weighted sum. The activation function is applied after the net input is computed.

questions.text: Average-pooling reduces computations and is robust to background noise.
questions.feedback: Average-pooling reduces computations, but it is Max-pooling that is robust to background noise — not average-pooling.

questions.text: CNNs adopt automatic and hierarchical feature engineering, in which kernels are pre-computed inside the network.
questions.feedback: CNNs do adopt automatic and hierarchical feature engineering, but kernels are LEARNED (not pre-computed) during training.

questions.text: Why does a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) beat SIFT + traditional classifiers (SVM)?
options: It adapts to data, learns mid-level spatial features, scales with more data.
It augments data, learns mid-level spatial features, pre-computes kernel coefficients.
It adapts to data, extracts spatial features, underfits with more data.
questions.answer: It adapts to data, learns mid-level spatial features, scales with more data.
questions.feedback: CNNs adapt to data, learn mid-level spatial features automatically, and performance scales with more data — unlike handcrafted methods.

questions.text: In Max-pooling, as long as the feature activates anywhere in the input image, the output remains high.
questions.feedback: Max-pooling keeps the highest activation within its window — not anywhere in the entire image. It provides local, not global, translation invariance.

questions.text: The Max-pooling goal is to down-sample the learned feature maps to reduce computations and it always ignores the exact position within the window.
questions.feedback: Max-pooling down-samples feature maps to reduce computations and discards the exact position of the maximum within the pooling window.

questions.text: In a Gaussian filter, pixels closer to the center have ________ weight, and weights ________ towards borders.
questions.feedback: Gaussian filters assign higher weights to pixels near the center and weights decrease towards the borders.

questions.text: Extreme outliers applied to an image like random 'salt-and-pepper noise' are ________ because the median is ________ to outliers.
questions.feedback: Salt-and-pepper noise outliers are completely ignored by the median filter because the median is robust to extreme outliers.

questions.text: Noise is unwanted random variations in an image. Common reasons include:
questions.feedback: The lecture identifies quantization errors and sensor imperfections as the main sources of noise in images.

questions.text: In Handcrafted Features like SIFT, edge filters, and interest points, the feature extractor does vary for different tasks (detection and matching).
questions.feedback: A key property of handcrafted features like SIFT is that the same feature extractor is used across tasks — it does NOT vary per task.

questions.text: Chaining two edge detectors works as a corner detector; which means hierarchical feature building, where the network can detect patterns of patterns.
questions.feedback: While chaining detectors is related to hierarchical feature building, a corner detector is NOT simply two chained edge detectors in the way described.

questions.text: The more the box-kernel size, both the more the computations and the more the blurring in output image.
questions.feedback: Larger box kernels require more computations and produce stronger blurring in the output image.

questions.text: Stride controls ________, smaller stride ________, and larger stride ________.
options: The Kernel Size – preserves detail – compresses faster
How many Kernels – preserves detail – compresses faster
How much the kernel jumps – compresses faster – preserves detail
How much the kernel jumps – preserves detail – compresses faster
questions.answer: How much the kernel jumps – preserves detail – compresses faster
questions.feedback: Stride controls how much the kernel moves at each step. Smaller stride preserves more detail; larger stride compresses the output faster.

questions.text: In Handcrafted Features like SIFT, edge filters, and interest points, the key property is that it is not specific and is adaptive to data.
questions.feedback: Handcrafted features like SIFT are task-specific and NOT adaptive to data — that is a property of learned features in CNNs.

questions.text: The notation g[x,y] = Σ Σ w[s,t] f[x−s, y−t] represents which of the following in the context of computer vision?
questions.feedback: This double-summation notation — sliding a weight kernel w over image f — is the standard mathematical definition of convolution.
